title: Multi-agent systems: orchestrator, specialists and handoff

videos.script: One agent with every tool is the simplest design, and often the right one. This lesson is about when to split the work across several agents, and what the split costs. {{title}} There are two shapes. An orchestrator keeps the conversation and asks specialists questions, the way it would call a tool. Or a triage agent hands the whole conversation over, and the specialist answers the customer itself. {{shapes}} You will run both on Marginalia's questions. Then you will count. The orchestrator and its two specialists sent six requests where one agent alone sent two. {{count}} The interesting part is the boundary between agents. What crosses it is all the other agent will ever know. {{boundary}} You will watch an answer go wrong at that boundary. A specialist reads two orders, sums them up in one careless sentence, and the orchestrator tells the customer something false. Then the host attaches the evidence, and the same summary stops misleading anyone. {{telephone}}
